Do not \\\\\"fix\\\\\" a migrated skill by editing the leftover skill copy; that edit does not reach\\\\n   the agents now reading the memory.\\\\n\\\\n## Hard Rules\\\\n\\\\n- Create and delete apply only to custom (USER) skills \\\\u2014 managed (LEARNED) skills cannot be created or deleted from Chat.\\\\n- To edit a managed skill\\'s content, use `update_skill`. Do not show the ID.\\\\n5. **Ask the user to confirm** \\\\u2014 Use `ask_user` to confirm activation:\\\\n   ```\\\\n   ask_user(\\\\n     question=\\\\\"Would you like me to activate this skill?\\\\\",\\\\n     options=[\\\\n       {\\\\\"label\\\\\": \\\\\"Activate\\\\\", \\\\\"description\\\\\": \\\\\"Make this skill available for use\\\\\"},\\\\n       {\\\\\"label\\\\\": \\\\\"Keep inactive\\\\\", \\\\\"description\\\\\": \\\\\"Save the skill but don\\'t activate it yet\\\\\"}\\\\n     ]\\\\n   )\\\\n   ```\\\\n6. **On confirmation** \\\\u2014 call `activate_skill` with the knowledge_item_id to make it live\\\\n7. **The skill is now available** \\\\u2014 `create_skill` returns the skill content in its response, so you already have the instructions. Disabled skills remain in the agent space but are not loaded by agents\\\\n\\\\n### Change Agent Type\\\\n\\\\nWhen a user asks to change which agent types can use a skill:\\\\n\\\\n1. **Call `update_skill_agent_type`** with the knowledge_item_id and the desired agent_types list \\\\u2014 see the tool\\'s `agent_types` parameter for the accepted values\\\\n2. **Report** \\\\u2014 confirm the new agent type targeting\\\\n\\\\n## SKILL.md Format\\\\n\\\\nCreate a valid SKILL.md with YAML frontmatter and markdown body:\\\\n\\\\n```markdown\\\\n---\\\\nname: my-skill-name\\\\ndescription: Brief description of what this skill does. Example: `rds-throttling-investigation`\\\\n- `description`: Required. Brief explanation of when to use this skill (min 100 chars recommended, max 1024 chars).\\\\n\\\\n### Resource Files\\\\n\\\\nSkills can include reference files alongside SKILL.md. {"id": "9625e207-b29a-4bd0-90fc-70a56666306c", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "Here's what AWS documentation actually says — a couple of corrections to the framing of your question, since there's no skill in your agent space on this topic and I don't want to invent a specific breakeven-hours number that isn't backed by a source:

**There's no fixed "breakeven hours per month" published by AWS.** MediaLive reservations work differently than a simple hours threshold would suggest:

- A reservation is a **one-year commitment** (billed monthly) to a specific input/output configuration — resolution, codec, bitrate tier, region, etc.
- You pay a reduced **hourly rate for a pool of minutes per month** (up to 60 minutes/hour, replenished monthly).
- Because the discounted rate only applies to matching inputs/outputs that are actually running, whether a reservation "beats" on-demand depends entirely on **how close your actual monthly running hours are to ~730 hours (24/7 for the month)** and how the reserved hourly rate compares to the on-demand rate for that same configuration — both of which vary by channel class, resolution, codec, and region. There's no single universal hour count; it's a per-config price comparison you'd need to run against the current MediaLive price list for your specific setup.

**Why unused reserved hours are a risk** — this part is explicit in AWS's docs:
- Reservation minutes are allocated monthly, and **any unused minutes in a given month are lost — they do not roll over** to the next month.
